en: We had a look at stacks and queues and list
and map-like structures in general. Now in
this module,
we're going to have a look at trees.
Obviously not the trees that you find in a
park or in the woods. Instead, we'll have a
look at tree data structures. Data
structures that work with depth and with
relations to express data.
And whilst this might sound very abstract,
you will learn throughout this module that
there are a lot of scenarios and use cases
where we actually work with a tree in
programming or where using tree structures
could help us solve certain problems.
Specifically in this module, we're of course
going to have a look at what tree structures
are, why we would use them and how they
work.
And we'll build a tree, of course. We'll
build multiple trees, but we'll start with a
pretty straightforward simple one,
and we'll then dive into more specialized
trees that optimize certain aspects or solve
certain problems in a better way. We'll have
a look at the binary search tree data
structure and the AVL tree data structure,
and I'll explain what those trees are about,
why they exist, how they work, and how they
differ from each other.
And we'll then also have a look at so-called
tries, and I will explain what that is
and when and how to use those.
So let's jump right in.
